The patient's age of 50 years, while intermediate, is more typical for IDH-wildtype than IDH-mutant gliomas. The combination of these features is highly characteristic of glioblastoma, IDH-wildtype. There are no features, such as ill-defined borders or minimal enhancement, to suggest an IDH-mutant tumor.

This tumor demonstrates a substantial necrotic volume (NCR Volume (mL) of 9.265) and marked, thick ring enhancement. These features are definitive for a Grade 4 tumor. Other features of high-grade malignancy, such as deep white matter and ependymal invasion, further support this conclusion. There is no evidence to suggest a lower grade.
